target_customer: Consumers, especially Gen Z and young travelers, who want airline miles without relying on a premium credit card
problem: Earning transferable airline miles usually requires premium credit cards and juggling many loyalty programs. Rove pools earning across hotels, shopping and dining into one mile that transfers to airlines.
business_model: Affiliate and hotel commission share: merchants pay Rove commissions and Rove passes part to users as miles; margin retained
product_category: Travel rewards and universal airline mile

founders.name: Max Morganroth
previous_startups: Startup founded at Wharton (details not given)
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch in May 2025 says he is 22.

founders.name: Arhan Chhabra
education: Harvard, CS and Economics, dropped out per TechCrunch
previous_startups: Startup founded at Harvard (details not given)
founders.background_notes: YC launch post says the founders started companies at Wharton and Harvard without saying which founder led which.

competitors.name: Rocketmiles
competitors.what: Earn miles or points on hotel bookings without a special card
competitors.traction_then: Established, later part of Agoda per its own blog

competitors.name: Rakuten
competitors.what: Shopping cashback via affiliate links, which TechCrunch compares to Rove's shopping model

technical_complexity.rationale: Chrome extension, affiliate integrations and airline loyalty transfer partnerships; the hard part is business development with airlines rather than engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Affiliate and hotel commission inventory is widely available and airline transfer deals are the main differentiator; cards and incumbents can copy the earning side.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent acquisition or copy was found through the sources reviewed.

market_need_then: Travel loyalty is large and card-driven; the founders said they flew to dozens of countries using points. The offer targets people without premium cards. Demand evidence is mostly founder claims and travel blog coverage.

branding.domain_note: Product site is rovemiles.com per TechCrunch; the YC listing uses rove.com. Many unrelated companies are called Rove.

identity.logo: Rove logo with hotel photos and airline logos on the site
identity.voice_and_tone: Upbeat, benefit-focused, short headlines such as Travel the world for free

branding.community_and_virality: Covered by travel blogs such as View from the Wing and PhocusWire; no merch or fan accounts found.

brand_strength.rationale: Repeated coverage in miles and points press and a distinctive product name for the currency, but the base word is generic and shared with other companies.

outcome_analysis: Rove is an active YC Winter 2024 company that launched its universal airline mile publicly in May 2025 with partnerships across about 11 airlines and has since added dining, an app and gift cards. It raised about 2 million USD. No shutdown or exit was found. Success depends on airline partnerships and affiliate economics.
notes: Round date not stated by TechCrunch. CB Insights total 2.5M USD seen only in a snippet, unverified. Another aggregator shows a Caplight seed dated March 2026, unclear. Many other companies are named Rove; entries for those were ignored.
